inputs.text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as another budget shortfall threatens more than 70 positions. That apology says a lot about how families are left to absorb the guilt and worry created by chronic underinvestment. These cuts aren’t just numbers: they put workers’ livelihoods and students’ access to support at risk. Schools need sustained public investment, not a system that makes staff and children bear the cost of institutional failure.
